newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria elects c.bank deputy governors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria elects c.bank deputy governors.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament elected on Friday three deputy governors to head the central bank departments that will play key role in implementing an IMF-prescribed currency board system from July 1.

Parliament approved the candidates proposed by the Bulgarian National Bank governor Svetoslav Gavriiski, who was appointed on Wednesday, with 180 votes for, one against and 27 abstentions from 207 deputies present.

Martin Zaimov, 35, will head the Issue Department that will implement the currency board, overseeing that levs in circulation are fully matched by foreign exchange reserves estimated at around $1 billion at the time of introduction and never provides credit to any account holder.
Zaimov served as deputy trade minister in the interim cabinet which stepped down in April and then as finance advisor to the reformist cabinet led by Ivan Kostov.

Valentin Tsvetanov, 37, will head the Banking Department which manages the lender of last resort role and reserve requirements for commercial banks with the aim of ensuring the functioning of financial markets.
Tsvetanov so far served as director of the Bank Consolidation Company, which manages state equity in local commericial banks.

Emilia Milanova, 45, will head the Bank Supervision department which enforces prudential regulations and banking laws to ensure soundness of the banking system. Milanova has so far served as auditor of the state Biochim Bank, Elitbank, Balkanbank and the Private Agricultural Investment Bank.
The remaining three members of the seven-member BNB board are to be appointed by the president.

Parliament has yet to pass this year's budget and a Banking Law to complete preparations for launching the currency board system designed to restore confidence in the weak currency and banks. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
